name: Optical & eye care (category guide)
summary: Optometrist vs ophthalmologist triage for foreigners — mall refraction vs disease workups, OOB registration checks, and when polyclinic referral beats Specsavers-speed.
body: Mall optometrists are for refraction, contact-lens fittings, and routine spectacle updates — not for sudden vision loss, eye pain, flashes/floaters, or suspected disease. Optometrists and opticians must be registered with the Optometrists & Opticians Board (OOB); ask for the name on the register if a chain desk is vague. Disease workups belong with an ophthalmologist, usually via polyclinic or private GP referral (Singapore National Eye Centre and hospital eye departments are the public anchors). Foreigners pay unsubsidised rates on public pathways; private eye clinics bill cash/card unless your group plan lists outpatient ophthalmology. Corporate ‘optical benefits’ often mean a spectacle subsidy, not medical eye care — do not assume a retail voucher covers a retina consult. Bring prior prescriptions and any myopia-control history for kids; progressive and office lenses need real binocular testing, not a two-minute auto-refract. This is a category guide, not a ranked optical-chain list — verify OOB registration and insurer optical vs medical lines yourself. School photo seasons spike last-minute glasses fixes — dual-career families should keep a spare pair labelled in the school bag before class-photo week. Dual-career note: sticky-eye exclusion weeks need a named daytime adult and a written swim hold — see the pink-eye school-exclusion guide.
